newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Canal Plus welcomes Italy broadcast law.
newsitem.headline: France's Canal Plus welcomes Italy broadcast law.

text.p: A broadcasting law approved by the Italian parliament on Tuesday night provides a stable environment for pay-television channel Telepiu and will help a digital television platform to get started quickly, French pay TV group Canal Plus said.

"This law gives the pay television channel a stability which allows Canal Plus and Telepiu to pursue with confidence the development of the channel, which today has 850,000 subscribers," it said in a statement on Wednesday.

Canal Plus, which controls Telepiu, on Monday signed an accord for the development of a single digital platform in Italy with the groups which could have become its rivals in the field, public television group RAI, telecommunications operator Telecom Italia, and private companies Mediaset and Cecchi Gori Communications.

"The law also allows for a rapid development of an Italian digital platform, at a time when the talks already underway between Canal Plus and its Italian partners are progressing in a very constructive way," Canal Plus said.
The Italian parliament on Tuesday approved a controversial bill to create a watchdog body to oversee the telecommunications and television sectors.

The much-delayed law opens the way for the privatisation later this year of state-controlled telecoms group Telecom Italia and ends months of bitter argument over the future development of Italy's lucrative television market.
Under the terms of the law, a broadcasting and telecoms regulatory authority will be set up in September.
The law also stipulates that no single television company will be allowed to control more than 20 percent of television broadcasting nor more than 30 percent of revenues. WEM/SLA
